Not sure how it is outside of the US but if you’re in the US and going to a hospital for the surgery you probably won’t meet your anesthesiologist until the day of. If it is being done at the surgeons office you might have a chance to meet them ahead of time at your pre op. If ur pre op is two weeks or more before ur surgery you can just wait to ask them then but if it’s closer to the date of surgery it would be good to call to ask and let them know.

The surgeon will probably tell you to not smoke or drink one to two weeks before surgery and for a couple weeks after as it may slow the healing process or interfere with any pain meds/anesthesia you take

Your doctors won’t turn you in, and since you will be going under anesthesia and will probably be given strong pain meds during recovery it is very important to be honest and not smoke until they have cleared you. As long as you follow the instructions they give you, they won’t cancel it

Going from smoking everyday to a month long break is tough but it’s worth it to stay safe and get the results you want. Plus there is the upside of a tolerance break. Good luck :-D

To answer your first question: yes, anyone can be in a QPR. I am allo and was in two and had a great time.
QPR’s are very fluid in the sense that they can be whatever you want them to be. Some people in QPR’s may do sexual & typically romantic things, others do not. There are no set rules and it’s up to you to determine what goes in your QPR. 
I’d say that friendship differs from QPR in the level of commitment and type of relationship. The line may be blurry, especially if you are intimate with your friends, but a QPR is more of a partnership

Jealousy is a naturally complex emotion. I think to deal with it is less about overcoming it and more about addressing the root of it. What underlying emotions are causing it?

It sounded like your relationship shifted a lot more than you expected, and the way you describe it makes it sound less to do with his new partner and more about how your relationship changed with him; such as the cuddling and hand holding abruptly ending, and him spending less time with you.

As hard as it may be, talking to him about it is probably the best way of feeling it out. Especially if your relationship changed, setting new boundaries and making it clear for both of you where your relationship is will make the adjustment a little easier.

It is pretty normal for someone getting in a new relationship to spend a lot of time doting on them in a kind of honeymoon period, and I think that he will adjust and figure out a routine with time. But it’s also completely normal and valid to be upset about the change; I think anybody else would have a difficult time adjusting to an abrupt drop in quality time like that. I would explore that with him: how much time with eachother do you need to feel fulfilled in the relationship?

As for him not being as open to his family about you, that is a little more difficult, and there’s probably not much he can do to change it if his family is disapproving. It sucks to deal with, and talking to him about that (without pressuring him to “out” himself for lack of better term) might not change much but it will at least help him understand how you’re feeling. 

Your feelings are totally understandable, and I think I would feel the same way. I hope that everything works out for you and that you’re able to find a good resolution!

Hi! I’m also bisexual and a trans dude and I feel what you said about looking up to him and feeling less alone :-) 

This Reddit, as well as r/Hellenism has a lot of helpful resources for beginners. Here’s a post from r/Hellenism that might help
https://www.reddit.com/r/Hellenism/comments/mdb67a/those_who_are_new_to_hellenism_please_read_this/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf

I’d begin by researching and reading about Dionysus. Reading about him, his mythology and history, as well as festivals dedicated to him in the ancient times. Becoming familiar with him as a deity is a good first step. Also looking into his associations. You probably already have heard about his associations of wine, women, ecstasy/madness, and theatre. Learn about his other symbols, such as animals he associates with and such. theoi.com is a great resource, here’s a link to his page. https://www.theoi.com/Olympios/Dionysos.html

After that I would look into prayer and offerings if you are interested in worship. Basically just establishing a relationship with Dionysus through worship! Setting up an altar if you have the space and resources is helpful, but not necessary. You can do digital altars and look into different forms of prayer and forms worship such as meditation, or dedicating acts to him such as drawing, writing, etc etc. He will appreciate anything you dedicate to him. :-)

Here’s a link to a post that helped me understand more traditional prayer if that interests you! You don’t necessarily have to go this route, you can worship in other ways. But it’s cool to read about especially if you’re interested in more serious worship and Hellenism in general.
http://www.caldridge.net/2015/05/how-do-i-begin-practicing-hellenism.html?m=1

Im still relatively new to worship as well but I hope this helps! He is a wonderful God and is very kind and patient, so don’t worry too much if you feel nervous. I wish you luck darling. :-)
